pages.caption: My father had a small estate in Nottinghamshire, and I was the third of four
sons.
He sent me to Cambridge at fourteen years old, and after studying there three years
I was bound apprentice to Mr. Bates, a famous surgeon in London.
There, as my father now and then sent me small sums of money, I spent
them in learning navigation, and other arts useful to those who travel, as I always
believed it would be some time or other my fortune to do.
pages.description: [wide establishing shot of believed time fortune]

pages.caption: Three years after my leaving him my good master, Mr. Bates, recommended me as ship's
surgeon to the "Swallow," on which I voyaged three years.
When I came back I settled in London, and, having taken part of a small
house,
I married Miss Mary Burton, daughter of Mr. Edmund Burton, hosier.
But my good master Bates died two years after; and as I had few friends
pages.description: [distant wide angle of good master bates]

pages.caption: my business began to fail, and I determined to go again to sea.
After several voyages, I accepted an offer from Captain W. Pritchard, master of the "Antelope,"
who was making a voyage to the South Sea.
We set sail from Bristol, May 4, 1699; and our voyage at first was very
prosperous.
But in our passage to the East Indies we were driven by a violent storm
pages.description: [wide establishing shot of passage east indies]
pages.scene: Ship driven onto a rock by storm

pages.caption: to the north-west of Van Diemen's Land.
pages.scene: Ship driven onto a rock by storm

pages.caption: Twelve of our crew died from hard labor and bad food, and the rest were
in a very weak condition.
On the 5th of November, the weather being very hazy, the seamen spied a rock
within 120 yards of the ship; but the wind was so strong that we were
driven straight upon it, and immediately split.
Six of the crew, of whom I was one, letting down the boat, got clear
pages.scene: Men lower the boat and escape

pages.caption: of the ship, and we rowed about three leagues, till we could work no longer.
pages.scene: Men lower the boat and escape

pages.caption: We therefore trusted ourselves to the mercy of the waves; and in about half an
hour the boat was upset by a sudden squall.
What became of my companions in the boat, or those who escaped on the rock
or were left in the vessel, I cannot tell; but I conclude they were all
pages.description: [sweeping panoramic view of left vessel cannot]

pages.caption: lost.
For my part, I swam as fortune directed me, and was pushed forward by wind
and tide;
but when I was able to struggle no longer I found myself within my depth.
I reached the shore at last, about eight o'clock in the evening, and advanced nearly
half a mile inland, but could not discover any sign of inhabitants.
I was extremely tired, and with the heat of the weather I found myself much
inclined to sleep.
I lay down on the grass, which was very short and soft, and slept sounder
than ever I did in my life for about nine hours.
When I woke, it was just daylight. I attempted to rise, but could not.
pages.description: [moment of change as woke daylight attempted]
pages.scene: Waking at daylight, unable to rise

pages.caption: For as I happened to be lying on my back, I found my arms and
pages.scene: Arms and legs tied to the ground

pages.caption: legs were fastened on each side to the ground; and my hair, which was long
pages.description: [face filling the frame legs fastened side]
pages.scene: Arms and legs tied to the ground

pages.caption: and thick,
pages.scene: Arms and legs tied to the ground

pages.caption: tied down in the same manner.
pages.scene: Arms and legs tied to the ground

pages.caption: I could only look upward.
The sun began to grow hot, and the light hurt my eyes. I heard a
pages.scene: Feeling something alive on my leg

pages.caption: confused noise about me, but could see nothing except the sky.
pages.scene: Feeling something alive on my leg

pages.caption: In a little time I felt something alive and moving on my left leg, which,
advancing gently over my breast, came almost up to my chin, when, bending my eyes
downward,
I perceived it to be a human creature, not six inches high, with a bow
and arrow in his hands, and a quiver at his back.
pages.description: [moment of change as arrow hands quiver]

pages.caption: In the meantime I felt at least forty more following the first.
I was in the utmost astonishment, and roared so loud that they all ran back
in a fright; and some of them were hurt with the falls they got by
leaping from my sides upon the ground.
However, they soon returned, and one of them, who ventured so far as to get
a full sight of my face, lifted up his hands in admiration.
I lay all this while in great uneasiness; but at length, struggling to get loose,
I succeeded in breaking the strings that fastened my left arm to the ground.
And at the same time, with a violent pull that gave me extreme pain, I
a little loosened the strings that tied down my hair, so that I was just
able to turn my head about two inches.
But the creatures ran off a second time before I could seize them, whereupon there
pages.description: [moment of change as creatures ran second]

pages.caption: was a great shout.
And in an instant I felt above a hundred arrows discharged on my left hand,
which pricked me like so many needles.
Moreover, they shot another flight into the air, of which some fell on my face,
pages.scene: Shower of arrows into the air

pages.caption: which I immediately covered with my left hand.
pages.scene: Shower of arrows into the air

pages.caption: When this shower of arrows was over I groaned with grief and pain.
And then, striving again to get loose, they discharged another flight of arrows larger than
pages.scene: Arrows and spears strike the leather jacket

pages.caption: the first,
pages.scene: Arrows and spears strike the leather jacket

pages.caption: and some of them tried to stab me with their spears; but by good luck
pages.scene: Arrows and spears strike the leather jacket

pages.caption: I had on a leather jacket, which they could not pierce.
pages.scene: Arrows and spears strike the leather jacket

pages.caption: By this time I thought it most prudent to lie still till night, when, my
left hand being already loose, I could easily free myself.
And about four yards from me, for more than an hour, there was a knocking,
pages.scene: Watching a stage set up nearby

pages.caption: like people at work.
pages.description: [face filling the frame like people work]
pages.scene: Watching a stage set up nearby

pages.caption: From this, one of them, who seemed to be a person of quality, made me
pages.scene: Gentleman of quality makes a speech

pages.caption: a long speech, of which I could not understand a word.
pages.scene: Gentleman of quality makes a speech

pages.caption: I answered in few words, but in the most submissive manner; and, being almost famished
with hunger,
I could not help showing my impatience by putting my finger frequently to my mouth.
pages.description: [distant wide angle of help showing impatience]

pages.caption: He understood me very well, and, descending from the stage, commanded that several ladders should
pages.scene: Hundred inhabitants bring baskets of food

pages.caption: be set against my sides, on which more than a hundred of the inhabitants mounted,
pages.scene: Hundred inhabitants bring baskets of food

pages.caption: and walked toward my mouth with baskets full of food.
pages.scene: Hundred inhabitants bring baskets of food

pages.caption: There were legs and shoulders like mutton but smaller than the wings of a lark.
I ate them two or three at a mouthful, and took three loaves at a
time.
I then made a sign that I wanted something to drink.
pages.description: [face filling the frame made sign wanted]
pages.scene: Gulliver asks for something to drink

pages.caption: They slung up one of their largest hogsheads, then rolled it toward my hand, and
beat out the top.
I drank it off at a draught, which I might well do, for it did
not hold half a pint.
pages.description: [moment of change as hold half pint]

pages.caption: They brought me a second hogshead, which I drank, and made signs for more; but
pages.description: [broad sweeping view of brought second hogshead]

pages.caption: they had none to give me.
After some time there appeared before me a person of high rank from his Imperial
Majesty.
His Excellency, having mounted my right leg, advanced to my face, with about a dozen
of his retinue, and spoke about ten minutes, often pointing forward, which, as I afterward
found,
was toward the capital city.
I made a sign with my hand that was loose, putting it to the other,
to show that I desired my liberty.
He seemed to understand me well enough, for he shook his head, though he made
other signs to let me know that I should have meat and drink enough, and
pages.description: [moment of change as signs let know]

pages.caption: very good treatment.
But when I felt the smart of their arrows on my face and hands, which
were all in blisters and observed likewise that the number of my enemies increased, I
gave tokens to let them know that they might do with me what they pleased.
Then they daubed my face and hands with a sweet-smelling ointment, which in a few
minutes removed all the smarts of the arrows.
The relief from pain and hunger made me drowsy, and presently I fell asleep.
pages.scene: Falling into deep sleep from wine

pages.caption: It seems that, when I was discovered sleeping on the ground after my landing, the
Emperor had early notice of it, and determined that I should be tied in the
manner I have related.
Five hundred carpenters and engineers were immediately set to work to prepare the engine. It
was a frame of wood, raised three inches from the ground, about seven feet long
and four wide, moving upon twenty-two wheels.
pages.description: [broad sweeping view of four wide moving]

pages.caption: Eighty poles were erected for this purpose, and very strong cords fastened to bandages which
pages.scene: Nine hundred men hoist Gulliver with pulleys

pages.caption: the workmen had tied round my neck, hands, body, and legs.
pages.scene: Nine hundred men hoist Gulliver with pulleys

pages.caption: Nine hundred of the strongest men were employed to draw up these cords by pulleys
fastened on the poles, and in less than three hours I was raised and slung
into the engine, and there tied fast.
Fifteen hundred of the Emperor's largest horses, each about four inches and a half high,
pages.description: [sweeping panoramic view of fifteen hundred emperor's]
pages.scene: Fifteen hundred horses pull the carriage

pages.caption: were then employed to draw me toward the capital.
pages.scene: Fifteen hundred horses pull the carriage

pages.caption: But while all this was done I still lay in a deep sleep, and I
did not wake till four hours after we began our journey.
The Emperor and all his Court came out to meet us when we reached the
pages.scene: Emperor and court come out to meet

pages.caption: capital;
pages.scene: Emperor and court come out to meet

pages.caption: but his great officials would not suffer his Majesty to risk his person by mounting
pages.scene: Emperor and court come out to meet

pages.caption: on my body.
pages.scene: Emperor and court come out to meet

pages.caption: Near the great gate, through which I could easily creep, they fixed ninety-one chains, like
pages.scene: Chains locked to my left leg

pages.caption: those which hang to a lady's watch, which were locked to my left leg with
pages.scene: Chains locked to my left leg

pages.caption: thirty-six padlocks.
pages.scene: Chains locked to my left leg

pages.caption: And when the workmen found it was impossible for me to break loose, they cut
all the strings that bound me.
Then I rose up, feeling as melancholy as ever I did in my life.
But the noise and astonishment of the people on seeing me rise and walk were
inexpressible.
The Emperor, advancing toward me from among his courtiers, all most magnificently clad, surveyed me
with great admiration, but kept beyond the length of my chain.
He was taller by about the breadth of my nail than any of his Court,
pages.scene: Emperor in golden helmet with sword

pages.caption: which alone was enough to strike awe into the beholders, and graceful and majestic.
pages.scene: Emperor in golden helmet with sword

pages.caption: The better to behold him, I lay down on my side, so that my face
pages.scene: Gulliver lies down to face the Emperor

pages.caption: was level with his, and he stood three yards off.
pages.scene: Gulliver lies down to face the Emperor

pages.caption: His dress was very simple; but he wore a light helmet of gold, adorned with
pages.scene: Emperor in simple dress with jeweled helmet

pages.caption: jewels and a plume.
pages.scene: Emperor in simple dress with jeweled helmet

pages.caption: He held his sword drawn in his hand, to defend himself if I should break
pages.scene: Sword drawn, nearly three inches long

pages.caption: loose;
pages.scene: Sword drawn, nearly three inches long

pages.caption: it was almost three inches long, and the hilt was of gold, enriched with diamonds.
pages.scene: Sword drawn, nearly three inches long

pages.caption: His voice was shrill, but very clear. His Imperial Majesty spoke often to me, and
I answered;
but neither of us could understand a word.
After about two hours the Court retired, and I was left with a strong guard
pages.description: [broad sweeping view of two hours court]

pages.caption: to keep away the crowd.
Some of whom had had the impudence to shoot their arrows at me as I
sat by the door of my house.
But the colonel ordered six of them to be seized and delivered bound into my
hands.
I put five of them into my coat pocket; and as to the sixth, I
made a face as if I would eat him alive.
The poor man screamed terribly, and the colonel and his officers were much distressed, especially
when they saw me take out my penknife.
But I soon set them at ease, for, cutting the strings he was bound with,
I put him gently on the ground, and away he ran.
pages.description: [passage of time with put gently ground]

pages.caption: I treated the rest in the same manner, taking them one by one out of
pages.description: [distant wide angle of treated rest same]

pages.caption: my pocket;
and I saw that both the soldiers and people were delighted at this mark of
my kindness.
Toward night I got with some difficulty into my house, where I lay on the
pages.scene: Lying on the ground for a fortnight

pages.caption: ground,
pages.scene: Lying on the ground for a fortnight

pages.caption: as I had to do for a fortnight, till a bed was prepared for me
pages.scene: Lying on the ground for a fortnight

pages.caption: out of six hundred beds of the ordinary measure.
pages.scene: Lying on the ground for a fortnight

pages.caption: Six hundred servants were appointed me, and three hundred tailors made me a suit of
clothes.
Moreover, six of his Majesty's greatest scholars were employed to teach me their language, so
that soon I was able to converse after a fashion with the Emperor.
The first words I learned were to desire that he would please to give me
pages.scene: Gulliver begs for liberty on his knees

pages.caption: my liberty,
pages.scene: Gulliver begs for liberty on his knees

pages.caption: which I every day repeated on my knees.
pages.scene: Gulliver begs for liberty on his knees

pages.caption: But he answered that this must be a work of time, and that first I
pages.scene: Emperor says it must be a work of time

pages.caption: must swear a peace with him and his kingdom.
pages.scene: Emperor says it must be a work of time

pages.caption: He told me also that by the laws of the nation I must be searched
by two of his officers, and that as this could not be done without my
pages.description: [broad sweeping view of two officers done]

pages.caption: help,
he trusted them in my hands.
I took up the two officers, and put them into my coat pockets.
pages.scene: Gulliver places officers in coat pockets

pages.caption: These gentlemen, having pen, ink, and paper about them, made an exact list of everything
they saw.
In the right coat pocket of the great Man-Mountain we found only one great piece
pages.description: [sweeping panoramic view of right coat pocket]
pages.scene: Right pocket: piece of coarse cloth

pages.caption: of coarse cloth, large enough to cover the carpet of your Majesty's chief room of
pages.scene: Right pocket: piece of coarse cloth

pages.caption: state.
pages.scene: Right pocket: piece of coarse cloth

pages.caption: In the left pocket we saw a huge silver chest, with a silver cover, which
we could not lift.
In his right waistcoat pocket we found a number of white thin substances, folded one
over another,
about the size of three men, tied with a strong cable, and marked with black
figures,
which we humbly conceive to be writings.
In the left there was a sort of engine, from the back of which extended
pages.scene: Left pocket: engine with twenty poles

pages.caption: twenty long poles, with which, we conjecture, the Man-Mountain combs his head.
pages.description: [passage of time with twenty long poles]
pages.scene: Left pocket: engine with twenty poles

pages.caption: In the smaller pocket on the right side were several round flat pieces of white
and red metal, of different sizes.
From another pocket hung a huge silver chain, with a wonderful kind of engine fastened
to it,
a globe half silver and half of some transparent metal.
This engine made an incessant noise, like a water-mill, and we conjecture it is either
some unknown animal, or the god he worships.
I had one private pocket which escaped their search, containing a pair of spectacles and
a small spy-glass.
My gentleness and good behavior gained so far on the Emperor and his Court, and,
pages.scene: Children play hide-and-seek in Gulliver's hair

pages.caption: indeed, on the people in general, that I began to have hopes of getting my
pages.scene: Children play hide-and-seek in Gulliver's hair

pages.caption: liberty in a short time.
pages.scene: Children play hide-and-seek in Gulliver's hair

pages.caption: I would sometimes lie down and let five or six of them dance on my
pages.scene: Five or six dance on Gulliver's hand

pages.caption: hand;
pages.scene: Five or six dance on Gulliver's hand

pages.caption: and at last the boys and girls ventured to come and play at hide-and-seek in
pages.scene: Five or six dance on Gulliver's hand

pages.caption: my hair.
pages.scene: Five or six dance on Gulliver's hand

pages.caption: The horses of the army and of the royal stables were no longer shy, having
been daily led before me; and one of the Emperor's huntsmen, on a large courser,
took my foot, shoe and all.
I took nine sticks, and fixed them firmly in the ground in a square. Then
I took four other sticks, and tied them parallel at each corner, about two feet
from the ground.
I fastened my handkerchief to the nine sticks that stood erect, and extended it on
all sides till it was as tight as the top of a drum.
pages.description: [passage of time with sides till tight]

pages.caption: And I desired the Emperor to let a troop of his best horse, twenty-four in
pages.description: [broad sweeping view of desired emperor let]

pages.caption: number,
come and exercise upon this plain.
Fortunately no accident happened, only once a fiery horse, pawing with his hoof, struck a
hole in my handkerchief, and overthrew his rider and himself.
But I immediately relieved them both, and covering the hole with one hand, I set
pages.description: [passage of time with immediately relieved covering]

pages.caption: down the troop with the other as I had taken them up.
And the Emperor was so much delighted that he ordered this entertainment to be repeated
several days,
and persuaded the Empress herself to let me hold her in her chair within two
yards of the stage.
I had sent so many petitions for my liberty that his Majesty at length mentioned
the matter in a full council.
pages.description: [sweeping panoramic view of matter full council]

pages.caption: It was opposed by none except Skyresh Bolgolam, admiral of the realm, who was pleased
without any provocation to be my mortal enemy.
However, he agreed at length, though he succeeded in himself drawing up the conditions on
which I should be set free.
After they were read I was requested to swear to perform them in the method
pages.description: [passage of time with read requested swear]
pages.scene: Gulliver holds foot in left hand

pages.caption: prescribed by their laws, which was to hold my right foot in my left hand.
pages.description: [distant wide angle of prescribed laws hold]
pages.scene: Gulliver holds foot in left hand

pages.caption: And to place the middle finger of my right hand on the crown of my
pages.description: [face filling the frame place middle finger]
pages.scene: Hand on crown of head, thumb on ear

pages.caption: head,
pages.scene: Hand on crown of head, thumb on ear

pages.caption: and my thumb on the top of my right ear.
pages.scene: Hand on crown of head, thumb on ear

pages.caption: But I have made a translation of the conditions, which I here offer to the
public.
I swore to these articles with great cheerfulness, whereupon my chains were immediately unlocked, and
I was at full liberty.
One morning, about a fortnight after I had obtained my freedom, Reldresal, the Emperor's secretary
for private affairs, came to my house.
He ordered his coach to wait at a distance, and desired that I would give
pages.scene: Gulliver holds Reldresal in his hand

pages.caption: him an hour's audience.
pages.scene: Gulliver holds Reldresal in his hand

pages.caption: I offered to lie down that he might the more conveniently reach my ear; but
he chose rather to let me hold him in his hand during our conversation.
He began with compliments on my liberty, but he added that, save for the present
pages.scene: Reldresal explains the war with Blefuscu

pages.caption: state of things at Court, perhaps I might not have obtained it so soon.
pages.scene: Reldresal explains the war with Blefuscu

pages.caption: For as to what we have heard you say, that there are other kingdoms in
the world,
inhabited by human creatures as large as yourself, our philosophers are very doubtful.
pages.description: [sweeping panoramic view of inhabited human creatures]

pages.caption: It is allowed on all hands that the primitive way of breaking eggs was upon
the larger end; but his present Majesty's grandfather, while he was a boy, going to
eat an egg, and breaking it according to the ancient practice, happened to cut one
of his fingers.
Whereupon the Emperor, his father, made a law commanding all his subjects to break the
pages.description: [moment of change as whereupon emperor father]
pages.scene: Law decreed to break at smaller end

pages.caption: smaller end of their eggs.
pages.scene: Law decreed to break at smaller end

pages.caption: The people so highly resented this law that there have been six rebellions raised on
that account,
wherein one emperor lost his life, and another his crown.
But these rebels, the Bigendians, have found so much encouragement at the Emperor of Blefuscu's
Court,
to which they always fled for refuge.
pages.description: [sweeping panoramic view of always fled refuge]

pages.caption: And now the Blefuscudians have equipped a large fleet, and are preparing to descend upon
us.
I desired the secretary to present my humble duty to the Emperor, and to let
him know that I was ready, at the risk of my life, to defend him
against all invaders.
It was not long before I communicated to his Majesty the plan I formed for
pages.scene: Gulliver forms a plan to seize the fleet

pages.caption: seizing the enemy's whole fleet.
pages.scene: Gulliver forms a plan to seize the fleet

pages.caption: I walked toward the coast, where, lying down behind a hillock, I took out my
spy-glass,
and viewed the enemy's fleet at anchor.
I then came back to my house and gave orders for a great quantity of
the strongest cables and bars of iron.
pages.description: [sweeping panoramic view of strongest cables bars]

pages.caption: Having thus fixed fifty hooks to as many cables, I went back to the coast,
and taking off my coat, shoes, and stockings, walked into the sea in my leather
jacket.
The enemy was so frightened when they saw me that they leaped out of their
pages.scene: Enemy leapes from ships and swims ashore

pages.caption: ships and swam ashore.
pages.description: [passage of time with ships swam ashore]
pages.scene: Enemy leapes from ships and swims ashore

pages.caption: Then, fastening a hook to the hole at the prow of each ship, I tied
pages.description: [distant wide angle of fastening hook hole]
pages.scene: Gulliver fastens hooks to each ship

pages.caption: all the cords together at the end.
pages.scene: Gulliver fastens hooks to each ship

pages.caption: Meanwhile the enemy discharged several thousand arrows, many of which stuck in my hands and
pages.scene: Arrows strike Gulliver's hands and face

pages.caption: face.
pages.scene: Arrows strike Gulliver's hands and face

pages.caption: My greatest fear was for my eyes, which I should have lost if I had
pages.scene: Gulliver puts on spectacles for protection

pages.caption: not suddenly thought of the pair of spectacles which had escaped the Emperor's searchers.
pages.scene: Gulliver puts on spectacles for protection

pages.caption: These I took out and fastened upon my nose, and thus armed went on with
pages.description: [sweeping panoramic view of took fastened nose]
pages.scene: Gulliver cuts anchor cables with knife

pages.caption: my work in spite of the arrows.
pages.scene: Gulliver cuts anchor cables with knife

pages.caption: Then, taking the knot in my hand, I began to pull; but not a ship
pages.scene: Gulliver pulls fifty ships toward Lilliput

pages.caption: would stir,
pages.scene: Gulliver pulls fifty ships toward Lilliput

pages.caption: for they were too fast held by their anchors.
pages.scene: Gulliver pulls fifty ships toward Lilliput

pages.caption: When the Blefuscudians saw the fleet moving in order, and me pulling at the end,
they set up a scream of grief and despair.
When I had got out of danger I stopped awhile to pick out the arrows
pages.scene: Gulliver picks arrows from his hands

pages.caption: that stuck in my hands and face.
pages.scene: Gulliver picks arrows from his hands

pages.caption: I then took off my spectacles, and after waiting about an hour, till the tide
was a little fallen, I waded on to the royal port of Lilliput.
The Emperor and his whole Court stood on the shore awaiting me.
They saw the ships move forward in a large half-moon, but could not discern me,
pages.description: [broad sweeping view of saw ships move]
pages.scene: Gulliver holds up the fleet cable

pages.caption: who, in the middle of the channel, was under water up to my neck.
pages.scene: Gulliver holds up the fleet cable

pages.caption: The Prince received me at my landing with all possible joy, and made me a
Nardal on the spot, which is the highest title of honor among them.
His Majesty desired that I would take some opportunity to bring all the rest of
his enemy's ships into his ports, and seemed to think of nothing less than conquering
pages.description: [passage of time with enemy's ships ports]

pages.caption: the whole Empire of Blefuscu.
pages.description: [wide establishing shot of whole empire blefuscu]

pages.caption: But I plainly protested that I would never be the means of bringing a free
and brave people into slavery; and though the wisest of the Ministers were of my
opinion,
my open refusal was so opposed to his Majesty's ambition that he could never forgive
me.
And from this time a plot began between himself and those of his Ministers who
were my enemies, that nearly ended in my utter destruction.
About three weeks after this exploit there arrived an embassy from Blefuscu, with humble offers
of peace,
which was soon concluded.
Having been privately told that I had befriended them, they made me a visit, and
paying me many compliments on my valor and generosity, invited me to their kingdom.
I asked them to present my most humble respects to the Emperor their master, whose
pages.scene: Gulliver asks permission to visit Blefuscu

pages.caption: royal person I resolved to attend before I returned to my own country.
pages.scene: Gulliver asks permission to visit Blefuscu

pages.caption: Accordingly, the next time I had the honor to see our Emperor I desired his
general permission to visit the Blefuscudian monarch.
When I was just preparing to pay my respects to the Emperor of Blefuscu, a
pages.description: [passage of time with preparing pay respects]

pages.caption: distinguished person at Court, to whom I had once done a great service, came to
my house very privately at night.
I put his lordship into my coat pocket, and, giving orders to a trusty servant
to admit no one, I fastened the door, placed my visitor on the table, and
sat down by it.
His lordship's face was full of trouble; and he asked me to hear him with
patience,
in a matter that highly concerned my honor and my life.
"You are aware," he said, "that Skyresh Bolgolam has been your mortal enemy ever since
your arrival,
and his hatred is increased since your great success against Blefuscu."
That you, having brought the imperial fleet of Blefuscu into the royal port, were commanded
pages.description: [moment of change as having brought imperial]
pages.scene: First charge: refusing to destroy Bigendians

pages.caption: by his Majesty to seize all the other ships, and put to death all the
pages.scene: First charge: refusing to destroy Bigendians

pages.caption: Bigendian exiles.
pages.scene: First charge: refusing to destroy Bigendians

pages.caption: Again, when ambassadors arrived from the Court of Blefuscu, like a false traitor, you aided
and entertained them.
Moreover, you are now preparing, contrary to the duty of a faithful subject, to voyage
pages.scene: Third charge: preparing to visit Blefuscu

pages.caption: to the Court of Blefuscu.
pages.scene: Third charge: preparing to visit Blefuscu

pages.caption: But Reldresal, secretary for private affairs, who has always proved himself your friend, suggested that
pages.description: [distant wide angle of reldresal secretary private]

pages.caption: if his Majesty would please to spare your life and only give orders to put
out both your eyes.
At this Bolgolam rose up in fury, wondering how the secretary dared desire to preserve
the life of a traitor; and the treasurer, pointing out the expense of keeping you,
also urged your death.
But his Majesty was graciously pleased to say that since the council thought the loss
pages.description: [wide establishing shot of majesty graciously pleased]

pages.caption: of your eyes too easy a punishment, some other might afterward be inflicted.
"I leave you," said my friend, "to consider what measures you will take; and, to
escape suspicion,
I must immediately return, as secretly as I came."
At first I was bent on resistance; for while I had liberty I could easily
with stones pelt the metropolis to pieces; but I soon rejected that idea with horror.
pages.description: [broad sweeping view of stones pelt metropolis]

pages.caption: Before the three days had passed I wrote a letter to my friend the secretary
telling him of my resolution.
And, without waiting for an answer, went to the coast, and entering the channel, between
wading and swimming reached the port of Blefuscu.
His Majesty, with the royal family and great officers of the Court, came out to
pages.description: [passage of time with majesty royal family]

pages.caption: receive me,
and they entertained me in a manner suited to the generosity of so great a
prince.
Three days after my arrival, walking out of curiosity to the northeast coast of the
pages.scene: Gulliver discovers a boat in the sea

pages.caption: island,
pages.scene: Gulliver discovers a boat in the sea

pages.caption: I observed at some distance in the sea something that looked like a boat overturned.
pages.scene: Gulliver discovers a boat in the sea

pages.caption: I pulled off my shoes and stockings, and wading two or three hundred yards, I
pages.scene: Gulliver wades to inspect the boat

pages.caption: plainly saw it to be a real boat.
pages.scene: Gulliver wades to inspect the boat

pages.caption: I returned immediately to the city for help, and after a huge amount of labor
pages.scene: Gulliver brings boat to the royal port

pages.caption: I managed to get my boat to the royal port of Blefuscu.
pages.scene: Gulliver brings boat to the royal port

pages.caption: Where a great crowd of people appeared, full of wonder at sight of so prodigious
pages.scene: People marvel at the great vessel

pages.caption: a vessel.
pages.scene: People marvel at the great vessel

pages.caption: I told the Emperor that my good fortune had thrown this boat in my way
pages.description: [wide establishing shot of told emperor good]

pages.caption: to carry me to some place whence I might return to my native country.
And begged his orders for materials to fit it up, and leave to depart--which, after
many kindly speeches, he was pleased to grant.
Meanwhile the Emperor of Lilliput, uneasy at my long absence, sent a person of rank
to inform the Emperor of Blefuscu of my disgrace.
The Emperor of Blefuscu answered with many civil excuses. He said that as for sending
pages.description: [wide establishing shot of emperor blefuscu answered]
pages.scene: Blefuscu Emperor refuses to send Gulliver back

pages.caption: me bound,
pages.scene: Blefuscu Emperor refuses to send Gulliver back

pages.caption: his brother knew it was impossible.
pages.scene: Blefuscu Emperor refuses to send Gulliver back

pages.caption: With this answer the messenger returned to Lilliput; and I hastened my departure, resolving never
more to put confidence in princes.
In about a month I was ready to take leave. The Emperor of Blefuscu, with
the Empress and the royal family, came out of the palace.
pages.description: [wide establishing shot of empress royal family]

pages.caption: And I lay down on my face to kiss their hands, which they graciously gave
me.
His Majesty presented me with fifty purses of sprugs and his picture at full length,
which I put immediately into one of my gloves.
I stored the boat with meat and drink, and took six cows and two bulls
pages.scene: Cows, bulls, sheep, and rams loaded

pages.caption: alive,
pages.scene: Cows, bulls, sheep, and rams loaded

pages.caption: with as many ewes and rams, intending to carry them into my own country.
pages.scene: Cows, bulls, sheep, and rams loaded

pages.caption: Having thus prepared all things as well as I was able, I set sail.
When I had made twenty-four leagues, by my reckoning, from the island of Blefuscu, I
saw a sail steering to the northeast.
I hailed her, but could get no answer; yet I found I gained upon her,
pages.description: [moment of change as hailed get answer]

pages.caption: for the wind slackened.
And in half an hour she spied me, and discharged a gun. I came up
with her between five and six in the evening, Sept. 26, 1701; but my heart
leaped within me to see her English colors.
I put my cows and sheep into my coat pockets, and got on board with
all my little cargo.
The captain received me with kindness, and asked me to tell him what place I
pages.scene: Gulliver shows cattle to convince captain

pages.caption: came from last; but at my answer he thought I was raving.
pages.scene: Gulliver shows cattle to convince captain

pages.caption: However, I took my black cattle and sheep out of my pocket, which, after great
astonishment,
clearly convinced him.
We arrived in England on the 13th of April, 1702. I stayed two months with
my wife and family.
However, while in England I made great profit by showing my cattle to persons of
pages.scene: Showing cattle to persons of quality

pages.caption: quality and others.
pages.scene: Showing cattle to persons of quality

pages.caption: And before I began my second voyage I sold them for 600l. I left 1500l.
pages.scene: Gulliver sells cattle and prepares second voyage

pages.caption: with my wife, and fixed her in a good house.
pages.scene: Gulliver sells cattle and prepares second voyage

pages.caption: Then taking leave of her and my boy and girl, with tears on both sides,
pages.scene: Gulliver sails away on the Adventure

pages.caption: I sailed on board the "Adventure."
